sections.lead: We looked at your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Ding Ding already sounds like nobody else. The bio does not yet.
sections.keep: The caption voice. "It’s a tough life being a chopstick at Ding Ding." is a restaurant talking like a person.

title: Three things people
meet first.

pins.what: The bio's headline promises a twist on a category.
pins.why: "Reimagined" says what changed, but not into what. A guest cannot tell Ding Ding from the hotpot next door in five seconds.
pins.how: Name the one thing that is different, and let it lead the bio.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: People pick the closest hotpot, because nothing says why this one.

pins.quote: A is for Alaskan, still on the table at Ding Ding.
pins.what: King crab shows up again and again, and the bio never mentions it.
pins.why: It is the one dish nobody else leads with, so it works as the reason to choose Ding Ding.
pins.how: Make the crab part of how the brand introduces itself.
pins.label: Your grid
pins.cost: The signature dish stays a caption instead of the identity.

pins.quote: It’s a tough life being a chopstick at Ding Ding.
pins.what: Your captions are written in a real voice.
pins.why: Wit like this is hard to copy, and it sits in captions while the bio reads like a listing.
pins.how: Let the bio sound like the captions.
pins.label: Your captions
pins.cost: The best thing about the brand is only found by people who already follow.
